newsitem.title: UK: UK to approve BA-American link - report.
newsitem.headline: UK to approve BA-American link - report.

text.p: The UK government is set to approve the proposed alliance between British Airways and American Airlines, the Sunday Times newspaper reported.

The report said UK Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang would give the green light to the deal later this month. UK competition authorities are currently reviewing BA's proposed alliance with American Airlines, part of AMR Corp.

Citing "airline and Whitehall (ministerial) sources," the report said under the terms of the approval BA will surrender a number of take-off and landing slots at London's Heathrow airport to reduce its share of the transatlantic market.
The report added BA may also have to share Heathrow's Terminal Four, which it dominates, with other carriers.
The UK government approval would still leave two big hurdles for the alliance to clear.
The British and U.S. government have to agree an "open skies" deal that will open up Heathrow to U.S. airlines and provide liberalisation for British carriers in America.
BA and American must also win U.S. regulatory approval for the deal.
Under the planned link-up, BA aims to coordinate its 244 weekly flights from Britain to 22 U.S. destinations with American's 238 flights from seven U.S airports to 12 European destinations.
